title: Patch: rematch status refuses daily games and stale catalogs like rematch offers do

**Issue #4722 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4722: Patch: rematch status refuses daily games and stale catalogs like rematch offers do
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

After a game ends, the result screen asks the server whether a rematch is available and shows a Rematch button when it is. For a daily game, rematching means starting a new daily challenge, never a live rematch. After the cards change in a patch, no rematch can start until a new game is started. Right now the check that offers a rematch knows both of those, but the check the result screen polls does not, so the screen can offer a rematch that the server will then refuse.

## Why

`POST /api/matches/:matchId/rematch` refuses a daily game with 409 `daily` (`crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs:408-419`, SPEC §9.13: "a daily game's rematch is a new daily challenge"), and `offer_as` refuses a stale catalog through `check_offer` (`crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs:452-464`; `crates/shared/src/host/rematch.rs:77-92`, R1638000) before anything is recorded. `GET /api/matches/:matchId/rematch` (`rematch_status_route`, `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs:522-546`) only refuses series games, then answers the book's offers and the mode a rematch would play. The client polls that GET for the result screen (`apps/web/src/net/api.ts:1630-1638`; `apps/web/src/game/net.ts:437-438,651-654`, R3213000), so after a patch ships, or on a daily match row opened as a live match, it renders a Rematch button whose press can only fail with 409. Series already mirrors the POST refusal in the GET (`series_game` in both routes); daily and catalog do not. This is the same class as the fixed R4621000 daily-rematch handling (`apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx:19-20`), but on the 1v1 API rather than the daily board.

## Proposal

Make `rematch_status_route` return the same refusals `offer_rematch_route` returns: 409 `daily` when `daily_games_get` finds the match, and 409 `update_required` (via `cards_changed`) when the match's catalog differs from the server's, before reading the book. Keep the series-game refusal where it is. No change to the POST path, the book, or the sweep. Add server tests: GET on a finished daily match is 409 `daily`; GET on a finished match played on an older catalog is 409 `update_required`; GET on a current live-match finish still answers its offers and mode.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/api/rematch.rs` (`rematch_status_route`)
- `crates/server/tests/` rematch/status tests for the two new cases
- SPEC §9.1, §9.5, §9.13; R672, R1638000, R2685000, R3213000 (no new ruling: the decisions already exist, the GET just mirrors them)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] GET a finished daily match's rematch status answers 409 `daily` with the same message POST uses
- [ ] GET a finished match played on another catalog answers 409 `update_required` with matching `expected`/`received`
- [ ] GET a current-catalog live-match finish still answers 200 with `youOffered`, `opponentOffer`, `opponentHere`, `matchId`, `mode`
- [ ] New tests fail without the fix and pass with it; touched crate tests, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass

## Size and risks

Small: one route plus tests. Risk is a client that relied on GET succeeding for daily matches; the daily board never calls this GET (it uses `POST /api/daily/challenges`), so the only caller affected is the live-match result screen, which is exactly what should stop offering rematch there. Alternative rejected: leaving GET as a pure book read and hiding the button client-side by catalog version; that restates the rule in the client (CLAUDE.md rule 7) and would need the same check in every future caller.
```
